classification.difficultyReason: Uses two coordinate origins to model the same flight and selects the positive quadratic root.

content.prompt: A stone is thrown from the top of a 25 m building at 30 m/s at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Taking the origin at the base, find the time to hit the ground to 2 d.p.

answer.worked:
The initial velocity components are $\dot{x}=30\cos30^\circ=15\sqrt3$ and $\dot{y}(0)=30\sin30^\circ=15$ m/s. With the origin at the base, $y(0)=25$. At the ground, $y=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-5t^2+15t+25\\0&=-5t^2+15t+25\\t^2-3t-5&=0\\t&=\frac{3\pm\sqrt{29}}{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Taking the positive root,
$$t=\frac{3+\sqrt{29}}2\approx4.19\text{ s}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Repeat with the origin at the launch point and confirm the same time.

answer.worked:
With the origin at the launch point, $y(0)=0$ and the ground is at $y=-25$.
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-5t^2+15t\\-25&=-5t^2+15t\\t^2-3t-5&=0\\t&=\frac{3+\sqrt{29}}2\\t&\approx4.19\text{ s}.\end{aligned}$$
The same quadratic gives the same positive time.
